reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Validation of pre-April 8, 1994 corporate existence extensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1978 H.B. 1599 § 1, A.L. 1994 S.B. 600, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with H.B. 563 merged with S.B. 355, A.L. 2007 S.B. 22). Covers drainage, levee, or drainage and levee districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690 or 245.010 to 245.280 granted a circuit court extension of corporate existence prior to April 8, 1994, deeming full compliance unless set aside for good cause within ninety days after April 8, 1994.

headings.title: Ten-year period to reinstate and extend lapsed charters
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers the ten-year period after lapse of a corporate charter during which qualifying districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690 or 245.010 to 245.280 may reinstate and extend corporate existence by order of the circuit court having jurisdiction, deemed in full compliance with extension laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1978–2007 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked validation of pre-April 8, 1994 circuit court corporate-existence extensions for 242.010–242.690 and 245.010–245.280 districts unless set aside for good cause within 90 days in (1), and 10-year post-lapse reinstatement/extension period by circuit court order in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Petition and notice to reduce or cancel benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 S.B. 213 § 1). Covers petitions by landowners in state-law levee or drainage districts where subsequent improvements partially or wholly nullify prior assessed benefits, seeking reduction for maintenance-tax equity or cancellation, along with separate notice requirements for circuit court districts (service on president and secretary at least 30 days before hearing) and county commission districts (discretionary publication or other notice).

headings.title: Hearing decision, petitioner costs, and maintenance tax effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers court or county commission discretion to reduce, cancel, or deny the petition, requirement that petitioners bear all hearing costs regardless of outcome, and application of subsequent annual maintenance taxes to the reduced or cancelled benefits.

headings.title: Restriction while district has outstanding bond obligations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits reducing or cancelling assessed benefits under section 246.063 while the district has outstanding bond obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1959 history note; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked landowner petitions for benefit reduction/cancellation when subsequent works nullify prior benefits and separate circuit-court (30-day service) vs. county-commission (discretionary notice) rules in (1), discretionary decision, petitioner cost liability regardless of outcome, and maintenance-tax effect in (2), and absolute bar while district has outstanding bond obligations in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Tax anticipation warrants authorized by two-thirds acreage vote
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12613, A.L. 1953 p. 541, A.L. 1993 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 3, A.L. 1996 S.B. 671, Effective 2-13-96). Covers permissive issuance of tax anticipation warrants (up to 6% interest, 1 to 4 years maturity, payable from the maintenance fund) when authorized by owners of two-thirds of district acreage by ballot (one vote per acre) at a meeting under section 246.090.

headings.title: Landowner-voted 1993 or 1995 disaster notes (terminated 1998)
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes, including Revisor asterisk footnote ('*Authority to issue notes terminates 1-1-98') and subsection 6 termination clause. Covers supplemental authority for levee or drainage districts in counties declared presidential disaster areas during 1993 or 1995 to issue tax anticipation notes (up to 6% interest, 1 to 4 years) after two weeks' newspaper notice under 246.090(2) and a two-thirds vote of landowners present at the meeting; describes archived text without claiming current enforceability.

headings.title: Board-voted disaster notes (terminated 1998) and non-tax revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes, including Revisor asterisk footnote ('*Authority to issue notes terminates 1-1-98') and subsection 6 termination clause. Covers supplemental board-majority authority after two weeks' public notice in 1993 or 1995 presidential disaster counties to borrow and issue negotiable notes (up to 6% interest, payable from one year from issuance) from anticipated current or next-year revenues, plus the distinct final sentence stating all revenues raised by levee or drainage districts shall not be considered taxes under state law (whereas subsection 6 specifically terminates authority to issue notes under subsection 2 or 3 on January 1, 1998); describes archived text without claiming current enforceability.

headings.title: Disaster note principal limits and debt ceiling exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Covers capping aggregate outstanding principal of subsection 2 or 3 notes (notwithstanding section 246.080 or other statutes) to amounts necessary to repair levees damaged by a 1993 or 1995 natural disaster including securing federal matching funds, and excluding district tax anticipation notes from debt ceiling computations subject to that disaster-repair cap.

headings.title: Board certification of authority and prior unpaid notes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires the board clerk, secretary, or presiding officer to certify on the back of each note that it is issued under section 246.070 authority and list the aggregate principal of all prior unpaid notes against the district.

headings.title: 1998 termination of subsection 2 or 3 note authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and Revisor footnote ('*Authority to issue notes terminates 1-1-98'). Specifies that authority to issue notes under subsection 2 or 3 terminates January 1, 1998, without terminating subsection 1 warrant authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (6 subsections), 1953–1996 history notes (effective 2-13-96), and Revisor asterisk footnote ('*Authority to issue notes terminates 1-1-98.'); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked ongoing 2/3-acreage ballot warrant authority under 246.090 in (1), terminated 1993/1995 disaster landowner-voted notes in (2), terminated 1993/1995 disaster board-voted negotiable notes alongside the distinct general non-tax revenue characterization sentence in (3), disaster-repair principal cap and debt-ceiling exclusion in (4), back-of-note certification in (5), and Jan. 1, 1998 termination of (2) and (3) note authority in (6). Revised (2), (3), and (6) to surface the 1998 termination directly while keeping (3)'s non-tax revenue clause distinct from the terminated note authority; refined (3) reviewNote; retained (1), (4), and (5).

headings.title: Board order and form of warrant meeting notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, embedded statutory notice form table, and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12615, A.L. 1961 p. 463; prior revision 1929 § 11026). Covers board of supervisors entering an expediency and necessity order in the minutes for section 246.080 purposes and directing the secretary to prepare notice substantially in the statutory form (whose archived text refers to 'drainage district').

headings.title: Notice publication, landowner voting, certification, and warrant issuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers three weekly newspaper insertions (last at least 10 days before meeting), conclusive notice upon filing publisher proof of publication, voting one vote per acre or fraction, two-thirds district acreage threshold, teller certification, board record entry order, and subsequent warrant issuance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table (retaining archived 'drainage district' wording), and 1961 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked board expediency/necessity minutes order for section 246.080 purposes and substantial notice form in (1), and 3-week publication (>=10 days prior), conclusive publisher proof, one-vote-per-acre/fraction voting, 2/3-acreage threshold, teller certification, record entry, and warrant issuance in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: District purchase at tax sale and resale terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12609; prior revision 1929 § 11020). Covers authority of incorporated drainage or levee districts to bid up to taxes, assessments, interest, penalties, and costs at sales for their own taxes, sheriff conveyance, resale terms (free from or subject to prior taxes, continuing liability for subsequent taxes, and up to three-year installment postponement), and proviso against enlarging taxing powers.

headings.title: Form and execution of district deeds and conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Provides that deeds or other conveyances by the district shall be in the form and executed by the officers and manner determined by the district's governing body.

headings.title: Joint foreclosure purchases and 246.140–246.170 maintenance fund bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers agreements among multiple lienholding districts for one district to purchase land in trust at foreclosure sale, proportional interests based on taxes due, fixing rights of non-participating districts, and the final proviso prohibiting any expenditures or disbursements under sections 246.140 to 246.170 out of a district's maintenance fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and RSMo 1939/1929 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked district tax-sale bidding cap, sheriff conveyance, resale terms (including up to 3-year postponement and continuing subsequent-tax liability), and no-enlarged-taxing-power proviso in (1), governing-body deed execution in (2), and joint multi-district trust purchases, proportional shares, non-participating district rights, and the final proviso barring any section 246.140–246.170 expenditures from a maintenance fund in (3). Revised (3) to 'Joint foreclosure purchases and 246.140–246.170 maintenance fund bar' to reflect the cross-section reach of the maintenance-fund prohibition; retained (1) and (2).

headings.title: Authority to issue refunding bonds absent majority objection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 12611, A.L. 1945 p. 849; prior revision 1929 § 11022). Covers qualifying circuit court, county commission, reorganized (including 242.010–242.690), and 245.285–245.545 drainage or levee districts refunding outstanding bonds for terms up to forty years, conditioned on no hearing objection by a majority of owners owning a majority of district acres.

headings.title: Refunding bond limits, interest, exchange, sale, and proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers principal cap equal to refunded bonds, interest rate cap matching refunded bonds (payable semiannually), exchange by holder agreement or sale at not less than ninety-five cents on the dollar plus accrued interest, and restricting proceeds solely to paying outstanding bonds and issuance costs, expenses, and discount.

headings.title: Two-week landowner payoff right and pre-issuance tax preservation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers any landowner's right within two weeks after the refunding order to pay uncollected principal tax in full for release from refunding-bond taxes (while remaining subject to additional lawful taxes), and prohibits reducing applicable tax rates or assessments until refunding bonds are authorized and issued.

headings.title: Newspaper notice and hearing for proposed bond refunding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Covers notice by two insertions in a weekly newspaper in each county with district lands (last insertion at least five days before hearing) and holding the hearing before the board, court, or county commission.

headings.title: Statutory form of notice for bond refunding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5, embedded statutory notice form table, and history notes. Provides that notice to interested parties is sufficient if substantially in the set-out statutory form reflecting objection abandonment and the two-week principal payoff right.

headings.title: Deferred taxes, bondholder rights, non-paying landowners, and liens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Covers deferring original bond tax installments upon refunding, district duty to provide payment, preserving bondholder rights under incorporating acts, barring complaints over extra interest by landowners who did not pay off principal, and securing refunding taxes by the same lien as other district taxes.

headings.title: Exclusive procedure, broad applicability, and automatic charter extension
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Covers making section 246.160 proceedings exclusive, conferring necessary powers on past and future districts for past and future bonds, and automatically extending a district's charter life twenty years beyond the last maturing refunding bond when refunding bonds extend past charter life.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (7 subsections), embedded statutory notice form table, and 1945 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked eligible circuit-court/county-commission/242/245 districts refunding bonds up to 40 years absent majority-owner/majority-acre objection in (1), principal/interest caps, exchange or >=95-cent sale, and proceeds restriction in (2), 2-week principal payoff right and pre-issuance tax preservation in (3), 2-insertion weekly notice (>=5 days prior) and hearing in (4), statutory notice form in (5), deferred installments, bondholder rights, non-paying landowner bar, and tax liens in (6), and exclusive procedure, broad applicability, and automatic 20-year post-maturity charter extension in (7). Retained all seven drafted headings.

headings.title: Authorized investments for surplus district funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)), history note (L. 1971 H.B. 139 § 1), and cross-reference notes (70.377, 409.950, 369.194). Covers permissive investment of unneeded funds in direct or unconditionally guaranteed U.S. obligations, savings and loan accounts insured by the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation (retained historical reference), and FDIC-insured bank savings accounts and time deposits.

headings.title: Security under 110.010 and 110.020 for uninsured deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and cross-reference notes. Requires deposits in savings and loan associations or banking institutions exceeding FSLIC or FDIC insurance coverage (archived statutory text) to be secured as provided in sections 110.010 and 110.020.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(3)), 1971 history note, and 70.377/409.950/369.194 cross-references; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked permissive surplus-fund investments in U.S. obligations, FSLIC-insured S&L accounts (archived text), and FDIC-insured bank deposits in (1), and section 110.010/110.020 security for uninsured excess deposits in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: Prohibition on in-channel bridge supports and bank placement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (RSMo 1939 12441, 12444 [sic, section symbol omitted in source], A. 1949 S.B. 1086; prior revisions 1929, 1919, 1909). Prohibits persons, corporations, county commissions, and municipalities from placing posts, pillars, or piling inside district ditches, drains, or watercourses for bridges, trestles, or coverings, requiring supports on banks so water flow is unobstructed.

headings.title: Misdemeanor fines and daily penalties for unabated violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers misdemeanor conviction with a fine of $5 to $1,000 (retaining archived source spelling 'nor more then one thousand dollars') and establishes each day after thirty days post-conviction without abatement as a separate offense punishable by a $25 fine.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (2 subsections) and 1949 history notes (retaining omitted '§' before 12441 and archived spelling 'nor more then one thousand dollars' in (2)); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked ban on in-channel posts/pillars/piling by persons, corporations, county commissions, or municipalities and bank-placement mandate in (1), and $5–$1,000 misdemeanor fine plus $25 daily separate-offense penalty after 30 days without abatement in (2). Retained both drafted headings.

headings.title: County and municipal levee systems and eminent domain
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1993 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 3 § 1, Effective 9-30-93, and footnote '*Word "borrow" appears in original rolls.' on 'barrow*'). Covers permissive authority of counties, cities, towns, and villages to construct and operate levee systems protecting public facilities and residents' life, safety, and property, and to acquire local property, rights-of-way, easements, access roads, pumping sites, and barrow* and dredge disposal areas by eminent domain.

headings.title: Ten-mile extraterritorial power for certain first-class-county cities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Grants cities wholly contained in a non-charter first-classification county containing a University of Missouri campus authority, notwithstanding subsection 1, to exercise section 246.271 powers within ten miles of the city.

headings.title: Intergovernmental agreements under section 70.220
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes counties and cities, towns, or villages constructing or operating municipal levee systems to contract or cooperate under section 70.220 with other political subdivisions or state or federal agencies for levee construction, operation, repair, or maintenance.

headings.title: Municipal general revenue funding and general obligation bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Includes a municipal levee system as a public improvement under section 71.290 payable from general revenue and declares it a city purpose under Article VI, Section 26(c) of the Missouri Constitution eligible for municipal general obligation bonds subject to governing bond laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (4 subsections), 1993 history note (effective 9-30-93), and Revisor footnote ('*Word "borrow" appears in original rolls.' on 'barrow*'); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked county/municipal levee systems and local eminent domain in (1), 10-mile extraterritorial power for cities wholly in non-charter first-class counties with a UM campus in (2), section 70.220 intergovernmental cooperation in (3), and municipal-only general revenue (71.290) and Mo. Const. Art. VI, § 26(c) general obligation bond authority in (4). Retained all four drafted headings.

headings.title: Disaster-area revenue anticipation loans under section 140.015
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1993 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 3 § 3, Effective 9-30-93). Covers majority-voted borrowing by political subdivisions in counties declared major disaster areas under section 140.015 in anticipation of current or next-year taxes and revenues, capped at estimated revenue requirements arising from section 140.015, at up to 6% interest, payable within one year.

headings.title: Note certification, county treasurer registration, and cancellation recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires certification of section authority on the back of each note by the clerk, secretary, or presiding officer, fee-free registration with the county treasurer, and submission of paid and cancelled notes to record payment and cancellation dates.

headings.title: Exclusion for subdivisions with pre-September 30, 1993 authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Excludes political subdivisions already authorized under law existing prior to September 30, 1993 to borrow in anticipation of collecting taxes and revenues.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1993 history note (effective 9-30-93); verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked majority-voted revenue anticipation borrowing by subdivisions in section 140.015 major disaster counties (capped at 140.015 revenue requirements, <=6% interest, payable within 1 year) in (1), back-of-note certification, fee-free county treasurer registration, and cancellation recording in (2), and exclusion for subdivisions with pre-September 30, 1993 anticipation-borrowing authority in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.

headings.title: Assessed-benefit voting option for certain large charter-county districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1994 S.B. 633, A.L. 1996 S.B. 845, A.L. 2004 H.B. 795, et al. merged with H.B. 1207, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939). Covers permissive adoption (after a public hearing noticed under section 245.060) by levee or drainage districts with at least $25 million real property assessed valuation located wholly or partly in a charter county over one million inhabitants of an alternative voting rule granting one vote per $10,000 of assessed benefits (rounded down, minimum one vote below $10,000).

headings.title: Reapportioning levee installment taxes after section 245.197 readjustment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Covers permissive adoption (after a section 245.060-noticed public hearing) by any Missouri levee district to reapportion section 245.180, 245.190, or 245.198 taxes on identified tracts after a section 245.197 readjustment, add accruing bond interest, prepare a certified permanent Readjusted Levee Tax Record, and levy/collect annual installments under section 245.185.

headings.title: Reapportioning drainage installment taxes after section 242.500 readjustment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Covers permissive adoption (after a section 242.150-noticed public hearing) by any Missouri drainage district to reapportion section 242.450, 242.470, or 242.502 taxes on identified tracts after a section 242.500 readjustment, add chapter 242 bond interest, prepare a certified permanent Readjusted Drainage Tax Record, and levy/collect annual installments under section 242.460.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version (3 subsections) and 1994–2008 history notes; verified source identity and all fingerprints. Checked permissive assessed-benefit voting option (after 245.060-noticed hearing; 1 vote per $10,000, minimum 1 vote) for >=$25M valuation districts wholly/partly in >1M charter counties in (1), permissive levee installment reapportionment after 245.197 readjustment (245.180/245.190/245.198 taxes, bond interest, Readjusted Levee Tax Record, 245.185 collection) in (2), and parallel drainage installment reapportionment after 242.500 readjustment (242.150 hearing, 242.450/242.470/242.502 taxes, 242.460 collection) in (3). Retained all three drafted headings.
